<description>
## Motivation

`SignPSBTInput` currently rejects valid 65-byte Taproot signatures when `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` is absent.

A 64-byte Schnorr signature implies `SIGHASH_DEFAULT`, while a 65-byte signature carries an explicit sighash type. Without an input-level sighash constraint, both encodings are valid.

The existing check applies the locally assumed default to signatures that already specify their own sighash type. This can prevent valid Taproot PSBTs from being finalized.

## Changes

Update `SignPSBTInput` to accept valid 64-byte and 65-byte Taproot signature encodings when no explicit sighash constraint is provided.

Preserve strict sighash matching when the caller or PSBT explicitly specifies a sighash type.

Extend the regression coverage for Taproot key-path and script-path signatures, including mixed sighash types within the same PSBT input.

## Testing

Verified locally on macOS using AppleClang.

- Bitcoin Core build completed successfully
- `psbt_tests` passed with 10 test cases
- `rpc_psbt.py` passed after the key-path regression was added
- Mixed script-path regression added and awaiting local verification

The final script-path test must pass before the patch is considered ready for upstream review.

## References

Refs [[#36507](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36507)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36507)

The issue documents the original failure involving valid Taproot script-path signatures and an absent input-level sighash field.
</description>

[2026-10-18] c:6248468576 comment by julianvanceblackwood:
Thank you, @fametrano, for the detailed review and for independently testing the behavior against another implementation.

Your observation about consistency with SegWit v0 is well taken.

The current implementation distinguishes between an explicitly specified sighash constraint and an absent `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` field. The broader acceptance of valid Taproot sighash encodings was intentional, based on the per-signature semantics of BIP341 and the absence of an explicit input-level constraint.

That said, protocol validity and Bitcoin Core's existing finalization policy are separate considerations. I agree that introducing different default acceptance behavior between SegWit v0 and Taproot deserves careful justification, particularly when a narrower change may be sufficient to resolve #36507.

I will revisit the validation logic and regression coverage with your findings in mind, focusing on the distinction between `SIGHASH_DEFAULT`, explicit `SIGHASH_ALL`, and other valid Taproot sighash types when the input-level field is absent.

If limiting the implicit acceptance path to `DEFAULT` and `ALL` is the preferred policy, I am open to narrowing the patch accordingly while preserving strict checks for explicitly specified sighash types.

I appreciate the concrete reproduction and technical feedback. My priority is to deliver a minimal, well-tested change that addresses the reported interoperability issue without introducing unnecessary behavioral differences.

Thank you again for taking the time to review this.
